messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failure report indicates that unpacking a CPIO archive leads to an unexpected EOF exception. The test `testCpioUnarchive` creates a CPIO archive with two files and then attempts to read them back using `CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry`. The relevant `getNextCPIOEntry` method processes archive entries by first reading magic bytes to identify the archive format, then parsing entries accordingly. If the magic bytes don't match expected values, an IOException is thrown.

The reading logic in `read(byte[], int, int)` shows that after reading the expected size of data for an entry, the input stream is padded to align on boundary bytes based on format (new entries on 4-byte boundaries, old ones on 2-byte). Then, the method marks end-of-file for the entry and verifies CRC if applicable.

The `closeEntry` method consumes remaining data until the entry's content is fully read, setting an EOF flag afterward.

Considering the bug report about unexpected EOF during unpacking—even archives created by external tools—it is likely that the input stream reading and padding logic is incorrectly implemented. This can cause the input stream pointer to not advance correctly over entry data and trailer padding, leading to an incorrect EOF or truncation detection when reading the next entry's magic bytes.

The recent bug report about "getNextEntry() method doesn't skip over data fields correctly" in an old Tar implementation is relevant as it describes similar symptoms and suggests that the skipping/padding logic is critical and error-prone.

In summary, the root issue is the padding and entry skipping in `read(byte[], int, int)` and possibly `closeEntry()`. When reading entries, padding should be properly skipped for all formats, and the stream position must be correctly updated before reading the next entry's magic. If this is mishandled, it could cause the reported EOF exceptions when reading successive entries or externally generated CPIO archives.

The failing test invokes code paths that trigger this issue since it creates multiple entries in the archive and reads them back in sequence. The EOF would happen when the stream position is incorrect after the first entry.

Thus, the defect lies in the padding calculation and skipping logic in `CpioArchiveInputStream` when reading and finishing entries.

Next, I will suggest the most appropriate methods for fixing this problem.
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioArchiveInputStream.closeEntry()

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
